summary: PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication configured across the 3-node CentOS Stream 10 cluster: node1 is the writable primary, node2 and node3 are read-only hot standbys built via pg_basebackup with a dedicated replicator role. Data committed on node1 is confirmed visible on both standbys, and standbys reject writes. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (standbys first, primary last) with confirmed boot-id changes and full post-restart recovery of PostgreSQL, replication streaming, and data.
actions_performed: Inspected all 3 nodes (CentOS Stream 10, no prior PostgreSQL) and installed postgresql-server 16 on node1, node2, node3

Initialized the primary DB on node1 (postgresql-setup --initdb) and configured postgresql.conf (wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, hot_standby) and pg_hba.conf (scram-sha-256 host entries for replicator and general access from 10.100.255.0/24)
Started PostgreSQL on node1; opened firewalld port 5432/tcp (blocking cross-node access) and reloaded
Generated a replication password on node1 via openssl and created role 'replicator' with REPLICATION LOGIN, passing the password only via secret_env
Wiped node2/node3 data dirs and ran pg_basebackup -R against node1 to clone each as a standby (standby.signal + primary_conninfo auto-configured), then started PostgreSQL on both
Verified pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both standbys streaming/async, and pg_is_in_recovery()=true on node2/node3
Created repl_test table and inserted a row on node1; confirmed the row appeared on node2 and node3, and confirmed both standbys reject INSERTs (read-only)
Captured pre-restart boot_id + health baseline on all 3 nodes
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified postgresql active, standby recovery mode true, and replicated data intact
Restarted node3 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified postgresql active, standby recovery mode true, and replicated data intact
Confirmed primary still streaming to both reconnected standbys before restarting it

Restarted node1 (primary) via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified postgresql active, primary (not in recovery), inserted a new row, confirmed both standbys reconnected as streaming replicas and received the new row

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as writable primary with replication enabled
evidence.summary: node1 initdb, postgresql.conf/pg_hba.conf replication config, firewall port opened, postgresql started, replicator role created

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 configured as read-only standbys via streaming replication
evidence.summary: pg_basebackup -R clone from node1 on both nodes producing standby.signal/primary_conninfo, then postgresql started on both

evidence.requirement: Streaming replication actively working, standbys read-only
evidence.summary: pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both standbys streaming; pg_is_in_recovery() true on node2/node3

evidence.requirement: Changes committed on primary visible on both standbys
evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 appears on node2 and node3; standby write attempts fail with read-only error

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 45c22b1f, reboot ack, timeout/reset during reboot, new boot_id 864363ae confirmed changed, postgresql active/in-recovery with data intact post-restart

evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id fb2aa416, reboot ack, timeout/reset during reboot, new boot_id c9f0f919 confirmed changed, postgresql active/in-recovery with data intact post-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 (primary) restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state, replication resumed
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bccb87ac and pre-restart replication confirmed active, reboot ack, timeouts during reboot, new boot_id c54395b9 confirmed changed, postgresql active as writable primary, new write replicated live to both reconnected standbys
